historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(core): keep an asset's creation date across updates (#18643)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
An asset's `created` timestamp was reset on every update, so it always
equalled `updated` and the original registration time was lost. The
`Asset` constructor defaults `created` to now when none is given, so on
an update the incoming asset always carried a fresh timestamp and the
fallback to the stored one never fired. The stored date now wins, and
only `updated` moves forward.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/issues/10288.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(triggers): disambiguate colliding trigger picker labels by plugin title (#18667)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
* fix(triggers): disambiguate colliding trigger picker labels by plugin title

The "Add Trigger" picker showed the MongoDB trigger as "Mongodb Trigger"
(wrong casing) and rendered it identically to Debezium's MongoDB CDC
trigger, since both are indistinguishable in the picker.

Root cause: PluginController#toApiTriggerPlugin always set the trigger's
`title` to `triggerClass.getSimpleName()`, which is literally "Trigger"
for the vast majority of plugins (Kestra's convention names every
plugin's trigger class `Trigger`). The frontend's triggerCatalog.ts then
fell back to guessing a label from the last Java package segment
(`trigger.type.split(".").at(-2)`) and title-casing it via
formatPluginTitle's bare capitalize() - so io.kestra.plugin.mongodb and
io.kestra.plugin.debezium.mongodb both derived "mongodb" -> "Mongodb".

Every plugin already declares a correct, human-authored title in its
metadata/index.yaml (e.g. "MongoDB", "Debezium MongoDB"), surfaced via
RegisteredPlugin#title() and already used correctly by the main Plugins
page through Plugin#of(). Reuse that same source of truth instead of
guessing from the class package:

- core: add Plugin#titleFor(RegisteredPlugin, Class), resolving an
  element's title with the same subgroup-title precedence as Plugin#of
  (subgroup's own @PluginSubGroup#title, then the owning plugin's own
  title), so it also disambiguates same-plugin subgroups correctly.
- webserver: PluginController#toApiTriggerPlugin now surfaces this as a
  new `pluginTitle` field on ApiTriggerPlugin.
- ui: triggerCatalog.ts's triggerDisplayName() falls back to the new
  `pluginTitle` field instead of deriving a guess from the class package.

This generalizes to any two plugins whose Java package happens to share
a segment, not just mongodb vs debezium-mongodb.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(namespaces): apply a namespace file rename only once the server accepts it (#18533)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
* fix(namespaces): apply a namespace file rename only once the server accepts it

`renameItem` fired the rename request without awaiting it and then mutated the
tree on the next line, so the outcome was shown before the server had answered.
Renaming onto an existing name answers 500, and the tree still displayed the
rename as done until the next reload put the old name back. The call is now
awaited, the tree is touched only on success, and a failure surfaces a message
naming the attempted name.

The same function left any open tab for the file untouched. Tabs are keyed by
path, so the stale tab pointed at a path that no longer existed and clicking it
navigated to a full-page 404, dropping the user out of the editor. The tab is
now moved to the new path when the rename succeeds.

Moving the tab needs to know whether one was open, so the close handler
provided by `useFilesPanels` now reports whether it removed anything. While
adding that, its lookup went from a prefix test to an exact match on the tab
uid: uids are `code-<path>`, so closing `a.py` could close `a.python` instead
whenever the longer path was listed first. Covered by four new unit tests, two
of which fail against the prefix lookup.

`closeTab` was also injected 190 lines below its first use, relying on the
temporal dead zone never being hit; it now sits next to `openTab`.

Closes #18467
Closes #18468

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01WAUBiJTcC3ABYSnRiUiPzZ

* fix(namespaces): report a failed rename once, and block a duplicate submit

Review found the friendly error toast is a second surface, not the only one.
Every generated SDK call goes through the interceptor in `utils/kestraHttp.ts`,
which for any status other than 400/401 sets `coreStore.message` and renders it
as a non-auto-hiding ErrorToast. The backend refuses a colliding rename with a
500, so the user got a persistent raw "Internal Server Error: /path/..." next to
the readable one. The sibling drag path, `nodeMoved`, catches and shows nothing
for exactly this reason, so the precedent was the opposite of what was shipped.
`renameFileDirectory` now suppresses the global message; it is called only from
`renameItem`, and the byte-identical `moveFileDirectory` keeps the global toast
for the drag path.

Moving the dialog reset after the await also left the Rename button and the
dialog's Enter handler live while the request was in flight. The Enter handler is
not gated by the button's disabled state, so two Enters fired two renames of the
same path; the second failed because the old path was already gone, and the user
saw a failure for a rename that had actually worked. An `isRenaming` guard closes

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/issues/10150.

filters[labels][EQUALS]=x (and other scalar-value operations that need

AbstractJdbcRepository now rejects a scalar-value labels operation
that requires a key with InvalidQueryFiltersException (400), naming
the filters[labels][OP][key]=value form the caller needs. The
remaining UnsupportedOperationException throws in the six dialect
label builders are swapped to InvalidQueryFiltersException as well,
for direct repository callers.

While tracing the per-dialect operation support, flows' map-value
CONTAINS/NOT_CONTAINS (filters[labels][CONTAINS][key]=value) turned
out to hit the same 500 on all three dialects, even though executions
already supported it - closed by mirroring each dialect's existing
execution-side condition.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: feat(dashboards): recycle offscreen dashboard charts and cap their canvas pixel ratio (#18588)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Lazy loading in #18199 stopped dashboards from firing every chart request at once, but it only throttled requests - it never bounded memory. Charts stayed mounted for good once activated, so scrolling a large dashboard grew the number of live ECharts canvases monotonically until the renderer ran out of memory. Large screens hit it first: a canvas backing store costs width times height times the device pixel ratio squared, and a tall viewport activates most of the page in one go, leaving the 200px lookahead doing almost nothing.

Canvas-backed charts (Bar, Pie, TimeSeries) are now unmounted again once their block sits more than 1200px outside the viewport, and remount when it comes back. The gap between that and the 200px activation margin is the hysteresis that keeps ordinary scrolling from thrashing, and a recycled chart's placeholder inherits the height the chart had so content below it does not jump. KPI, Table and Markdown charts are cheap and hold their own page, size and tab state, so they stay mounted once activated.

Chart canvases also render at a pixel ratio capped at 1.5 rather than the full device resolution, which cuts canvas memory substantially on a retina screen for a difference that is not visible on flat fills and thin lines. Activation is spread across frames, four charts at a time, so a tall viewport no longer mounts its whole first screen in a single long task.

Measured on a 30-chart dashboard at 2560x1400 with a device pixel ratio of 2, scrolling from top to bottom: canvas backing store drops from 57.2MB to 10.7MB and live canvases from 12 to 4, while at first paint the canvas cost drops from 19.1MB to 7.3MB. The JS heap is essentially unchanged, which is expected - canvas backing stores are allocated outside the JS heap, and that is the memory the tab actually runs out of.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/14234.
Related to https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/pull/18199.

fix(core): bound Pebble's range() function to prevent heap exhaustion (#18555)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
* fix(core): bound Pebble's range() function to prevent heap exhaustion

Pebble's built-in range() eagerly materializes an ArrayList before returning,
so an expression like {{ range(0, 2000000000) }} allocates billions of boxed
entries and OOMs the JVM. Any endpoint that renders a user-supplied Pebble
expression against a real RunContext is exposed, including the execution
eval debug endpoint. BoundedRangeFunction overrides Pebble's range() in
Kestra's Extension bean, computing the requested size upfront and failing
with a bounded PebbleException (surfaced as a normal render error) instead
of delegating once it exceeds 1,000,000 elements.

Closes #18418

* fix(core): bound Pebble render output size to prevent heap exhaustion

Point-fixes such as the bounded range() function and the indent/nindent
filters only close individual OOM vectors one at a time. The underlying
defect is broader: VariableRenderer.renderOnce catches
IOException | RuntimeException, so an OutOfMemoryError produced by any
other unbounded expression (a loop accumulating a huge string, repeated
concatenation, ...) is an Error that escapes rendering entirely and
crashes the JVM.

Guard the output at the writer chokepoint every rendered character flows
through: JsonWriter and TypedObjectWriter now enforce a configurable
kestra.variables.max-output-size (default 10 MiB) and throw a bounded
RenderLimitExceededException once it is exceeded. Because that exception
extends PebbleException, renderOnce maps it to
IllegalVariableEvaluationException - the existing graceful, non-fail-fast
render-failure path - instead of letting an OutOfMemoryError through.

Also centralize the existing single-shot pre-checks (range, indent and
nindent) onto a shared RenderLimits helper using the same exception type.

* fix(plugins): stop inlining icon bytes in the bulk plugin icon indexes

Cold-loading the Plugins page downloaded ~28MB, 24MB of it the icons
index, and parsing that on the main thread froze the sidebar router,
made the hover border trail the cursor by seconds, and left the page
sluggish until the load settled.

The bytes were never used. Both bulk indexes inline every icon as
base64, but the frontend keeps only the metadata (flowable, monochrome,
hash) and renders each icon from the per-class, browser-cacheable
GET /plugins/icons/{cls}/icon.svg. On a local instance the index is
6.36MB, of which 105KB (1.7%) is that metadata. So the indexes now
answer metadata only; `hash` is non-null exactly when a class has an
icon, which is what the frontend now derives `hasIcon` from. The
metadata view is itself cached, so the served map is a constant rather
than a per-request copy.

Splitting the caches fixes a second bug found on the way: Micronaut
derives a cache key from the method arguments alone, so the two no-arg
@Cacheable("default") index methods shared one key and whichever ran
first served both. GET /plugins/icons/groups was answering the
task-class index -- keyed by task FQCN instead of by plugin group.

Fixing that route exposed one behaviour to preserve: the group index
holds an entry for every group, iconless ones included, and callers read
mere presence as "has an icon". Those entries are now dropped client
side, so an iconless group keeps falling through to the ecosystem
catalog instead of rendering the generic icon.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/issues/10128.

no longer return icon bytes. The `icon` field stays in the response schema but
is always null on these two routes; fetch the bytes per class from
GET /api/v1/plugins/icons/{cls}/icon.svg, or read `hash` to tell whether a
class has an icon at all.

historicalFixesSummary.body:
* fix(executions): store total duration in milliseconds for Postgres state_duration

The Postgres executions.state_duration generated column used
EXTRACT(MILLISECONDS FROM interval), which returns only the seconds field of
the interval (0-59999) and dropped minutes and hours. Sorting executions by
duration was therefore wrong for any execution lasting one minute or more (a
7m run could sort below a 3m run). MySQL and H2 read the value as total
seconds and were unaffected.

Incremental migration 2.0.11 drops and re-creates the column using
EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM interval) * 1000, backfilling all rows, and recreates the
executions_state_duration index. The statements use IF EXISTS / IF NOT EXISTS
so the migration is safe to replay.

The fresh-install baseline (baseline-postgres.sql) is intentionally left
unchanged: editing it would change the '0-init' migration checksum and break
startup for existing installs (checksum validation throws on mismatch). The
incremental migration corrects fresh installs as well, since it runs on top of
the baseline. A regression test covers durations that straddle the one-minute
boundary.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix: bug-bash quick wins — page=0 SQL leak + Get Started onboarding link (#18552)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
* fix(webserver): reject page < 1 with 422 instead of leaking SQL on page=0

Pages are 1-based, and AbstractJdbcRepository maps a page to a SQL offset as
`pageable.getOffset() - pageable.getSize()`, which assumes page >= 1. page=0
produced a negative OFFSET, so the query threw and the raw SQL (table/column
names) was returned in the 500 body — on /users, /credentials and any list endpoint.

Guard page < 1 in PageableUtils.from (alongside the existing size cap) so it is
rejected with a clean 422 before any query is built.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/issues/10223.

* fix(flows): make the "Get Started" onboarding card link to the quickstart guide

The card had an empty link, so OverviewCard rendered a non-clickable <div> with

quickstart guide so it behaves like the others.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(flows): deduplicate the flow editor's Add-a-trigger panel (#18566)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Clicking "Add a trigger" navigates with ?createTrigger=true, and
MultiPanelFlowEditorView's onMounted handled it by calling
actions.openAddTaskTab directly, bypassing the dedup check that
useNoCodeHandlers.onCreateTask already provides for the same tab type
from the no-code editor's own UI. Every click therefore opened a fresh
tab with a new cache-busted uid, and since panel state persists across
full page reloads (by design), the stale tabs never went away either -
reopening the editor and clicking "Add a trigger" again just piled on
another one.

Routing the call through onCreateTask surfaced a second, latent bug:
its dedup-key computation didn't default 'position' the same way
openAddTaskTab does ("after"), so a caller that omits position (like
this one) computed a key that never matched the tab actually created,
duplicating it every time regardless. Both defaults now agree.

Closes #18321

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(core): validate and fail-execution on out-of-range user durations (#18549)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Replaces the earlier saturation approach. An unbounded user Duration fed into
Instant/ZonedDateTime.plus() overflowed with an unchecked DateTimeException that
escaped the queue consumer and, under fail-fast, shut the whole instance down
(poison pill).

Two layers:
- Save-time validation: a new @DurationMax constraint (default 10 years) on the
  plain-Duration fields (SLA duration, retry interval/maxInterval/minInterval/
  maxDuration, TimeWindow window/windowAdvance) rejects absurd literals with a 422.
- Runtime guard: DateUtils.plusOrThrow throws a handler-caught InternalException at
  the SLA, Pause and retry arithmetic sites so the individual execution fails
  cleanly and the poison-pill message drains, instead of crashing the executor.
  The flow-trigger window computation is wrapped to log and skip (no execution to
  fail). This also covers Property<Duration> fields (Pause, LoopUntil) that can
  only be checked at runtime, and existing bad flows already on the queue.

Closes #18369
Closes #18421
Closes #18423

Co-authored-by: nKwiatkowski <nkwiatkowski@kestra.io>

worker. VariableRenderer.renderOnce only catches IOException |
RuntimeException, so the resulting OutOfMemoryError escapes rendering
entirely. Caps amount at 10,000 with a bounded PebbleException above it,

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(executor): fail only the execution when a Loop's values shrinks between iterations (#18564)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
* fix(executor): fail only the execution when a Loop's values shrinks between iterations

LoopExecutionEventMessageHandler re-resolves a Loop's 'values' expression
on every iteration but only bounded the next index against the stale
iterationCount captured at loop start, not the freshly-resolved list
size. If a child task shrinks the underlying source (KV, file, subflow
output) between iterations, list.get(nextIndex) threw an
ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException/NoSuchElementException that the handler's
catch clause didn't cover (only InternalException | QueueException |
IOException | FlowNotFoundException). The escaped RuntimeException hit
AbstractSubscriber, which treats any uncaught exception as fatal and
shuts the whole instance down - and redelivers the same poison-pill
message on every restart.

Bounds each re-resolved list/URI read against its actual size, failing
with a clear IllegalStateException when it shrank, and broadens the
catch to RuntimeException so any such user-data issue fails only this
execution instead of escaping to the queue subscriber.

Closes #18355

* fix(executor): fail the loop-values-shrink case via InternalException, not a broadened catch

Keep kestra.queue.fail-fast=true intact. The previous revision broadened the
handler catch to `RuntimeException`, which would also swallow genuine runtime
defects that fail-fast is meant to surface as fatal. Instead, throw the existing
handler-caught InternalException at each shrink/resolution guard so only this
execution fails (via handleFailedExecutionFromExecutor) while any other
RuntimeException still escapes and is treated as fatal. The catch reverts to the
original `InternalException | QueueException | IOException`.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(design-system): align alert icon with the first line of wrapped messages (#18547)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Element Plus lays the alert row out with `align-items: center`, so the icon was centred against the whole message block rather than the line it belongs to. Any `KsAlert` whose text wrapped left the icon low by half the overflow: 7px at two lines, 14px at three, 21px at four, and 10.25px for a title with a description. `KsAlert` also set the title to `line-height: 1`, which left wrapped lines with no leading at all.

Anchor the row to the top, restore the title's leading to `--ks-line-height-base`, and raise the glyph by half the difference between the icon box and one line of text so it centres on line one. The offset is derived from whichever element renders the first line, since Element Plus shrinks the title once a description joins it, so there are three cases: title only, title with description, and description only.

Single-line alerts with an icon keep their exact height, since the icon already drove the row's height there. Alerts with a title are 6-7px taller now that wrapped lines have leading.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/18548.
Related to https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/pull/10379.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(ci): skip contributor onboarding for authors who already have write access (#18573)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The organization membership check added in https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/pull/18349 never worked. The bot token is scoped to a single repository, so `GET /orgs/kestra-io/members/{username}` answers 404 for every author, and the step could not tell that apart from a genuine non-member. Every author was therefore classified as an outside contributor, and https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/pull/18569 got the "First PR merged" congratulation even though its author is an organization member with private membership. The welcome-on-open comment was skipped there only by luck, because the author had opened a pull request before and the pr_count guard caught it.

This reads the author's repository permission instead. `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{username}/permission` only needs `metadata: read`, which the repository-scoped installation token already has, and it separates the two populations cleanly: organization members inherit write access on the repository, while outside contributors only ever resolve to `read`. The call is no longer wrapped in a catch, so a token that cannot answer fails the workflow loudly instead of silently commenting on a teammate's pull request.

Related to https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/pull/18349.
Related to https://github.com/kestra-io/docs/pull/5414.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(core): render execution-updating task properties for each execution
historicalFixesSummary.body:
`SetVariables`, `UnsetVariables` and `Exit` are `ExecutionUpdatableTask`s: the
executor calls `update()` on the task instance held by its cached flow, so a
single task instance is shared by every execution of that flow revision.
`Property` memoizes its rendered value on the instance, so the value computed by
the first execution was reused by all the following ones whatever their inputs —
e.g. a `SetVariables` deriving a boolean from an input kept the boolean of the
first execution.

Skip the render cache in those `update()` methods, like it is already done for
the flowable properties used to compute the next tasks.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(core): stop number formatting from crashing for the pt_BR and zh_CN languages (#18395)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
getLang() returns the raw stored language code, and the underscore codes pt_BR and zh_CN are not valid BCP 47 language tags, so passing them straight to toLocaleString() made humanizeNumber() throw RangeError: Incorrect locale information provided for users running the UI in Brazilian Portuguese or Simplified Chinese. A new getLanguageTag() helper next to getLang() converts the stored code to its hyphen form (pt_BR -> pt-BR) for Intl consumers, and the html lang attribute now receives the same valid form instead of the raw underscore code. The moment and cronstrue call sites are deliberately untouched: moment wants its own lowercase-hyphen keys (already normalized in init.ts) and cronstrue's locale ids use the underscore form.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/18401.

Entering maintenance mode revoked the per-loop vNode assignments, but exiting
it only resubmitted the loops. As no vNodes rebalance is triggered by a
maintenance toggle, the assignments were never recomputed: the loops idled with
no vNode, and every trigger event was dropped with "Received trigger events for
a non assigned vNode", so already-registered triggers stopped firing and newly
saved flows never registered until the server was restarted.

The assignments are now restored before restarting the scheduling. They are also
distributed over the scheduling-loops that effectively exist instead of over
maxThreads, which orphaned every vNode whose modulo exceeded the number of loops
when a scheduler was assigned fewer vNodes than threads.

Closes kestra-io/kestra-ee#10013

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(logs): stop a stale search from replacing the logs list
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Related to kestra-io/kestra-ee#8205.

Entering `/logs` fired **three** page-sized searches: `KsDataTable` loads on mount, so the first ran against the bare query (no level, no time window — a scan of the whole log table), then the default time range landed, then the default level. Each round also fired 5 level-count probes.

`findLogs` published whatever came back, without checking the response still belonged to the newest search — so the last one to land won. When the broad search is the slow one, its late answer overwrites the correct result: the list shows rows the filters exclude, or nothing when the stale search matched nothing, while every request looks fine in the network tab.

Fix:
- `useRouteFilterPolicy` exposes `isRouteSettled`; `LogsWrapper` gates its first load on it → one search per page entry instead of three.
- The logs store drops superseded responses → covers the races the gate doesn't (filter changes, pagination, refresh).

Two unit specs, both failing on `develop` and passing here. Reproduced in a browser by delaying only the discarded searches: URL says *at or above INFO* (6 lines), list rendered all 9 including DEBUG; now stays at 6.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(executions): wait for all WorkingDirectory subtasks before terminating the flowable
historicalFixesSummary.body:
A WorkingDirectory runs all its subtasks in the Worker; each reports its
terminal result through an independent queue message. When one subtask
fails, WorkingDirectory (via Sequential/FlowableUtils) resolved to a
terminal state as soon as it saw the failure, without checking whether a
sibling's terminal message had been joined yet. The executor then force-
marked that sibling to the parent's terminal state, discarding its real
outcome and outputs.

This surfaced as a rare flake in WorkingDirectoryTest (t2/t3 output
missing depending on message-join ordering), reproduced on CI independently
of PR #18237, e.g. run 32038144489 on branch refactor/compact-2.0-migrations
a day before that PR existed.

Add a resolveState override on WorkingDirectory that defers to Optional.empty()
while any child taskrun is still non-terminal, so the flowable only resolves
once every reported subtask has actually finished.

for the second, and neither can tell them apart today. State neither cause:

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(scheduler): report a governance block in the trigger's own logs
historicalFixesSummary.body:
A trigger whose flow a governance policy blocks simply stopped firing. The
only trace was a server-side warning the user cannot reach, so the trigger
looked broken with no explanation. Report the block through the trigger's
run context, which is what reaches the UI: per skipped evaluation in the
fetcher, and once per declared trigger at initialization, where a blocked
flow never gets a trigger state and so gets no other report.

TriggerFlowParser now throws FlowBlockedException instead of returning null.
Its old contract encoded three outcomes in one nullable return: the parsed
flow, null for a governance block, and the same instance back for a degraded
parse. A caller could not tell a block from a parse failure, and had no
reason to report either. The checked exception hands over the reason and
makes every caller decide what to do with it.

captured at backfill creation was overwritten with the backfill position.
Deleting the backfill then restored that position, and the trigger replayed every

scheduler, indexer and controller all purging the same KV entries.

Both do cluster-global work with no component-local state, so one
component is enough. Introduce @RequiresExecutor — the executor-side
sibling of the existing @WebServerEnabled and @RequiresControllerServer —
and apply it to both jobs. Its defaultValue keeps the jobs enabled when

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(ui): default logs and editor font size to 12px at medium mode (#18071)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
* fix(ui): default logs and editor font size to 12px at medium mode

Logs and the editor now derive their base font size from a monospace
scale (11/12/14) instead of the interface scale (12/14/16), so the
medium mode renders at 12px.

Bump the one-time localStorage migration to _fontMigratedV3 to clear a
stale logsFontSize=14 left over from the old default for users who
already ran the v2 migration, without touching stored editor sizes
(12 now matches the new default).

* fix(ui): keep the one-time font migration at _fontMigratedV2

Drop the V3 migration bump. V2 already shipped, so a stored logsFontSize of
14 is an explicit user choice, not a leftover default; re-running the
migration would silently delete it. Keeping V2 handles both cases: users who
never ran it get their legacy defaults cleared and land on the new mono
values, while already-migrated users keep their choices.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(worker): fail the attempt that ran instead of adding one when the result is too large
historicalFixesSummary.body:
TaskRun.fail() appends an attempt, so a task whose result was rejected
reported a phantom second attempt and its error log landed on the first,
successful one.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(worker): log why an oversized task result was rejected in the execution logs
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Logs is a server-side logger, so the reason never reached the execution
logs and the user only saw a failed task run with no outputs.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(worker): log why an oversized job was rejected in the execution logs
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The controller failed the job before dispatch and logged the reason only
server-side, leaving the user with a FAILED task run and no logs.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: refactor(executions)!: prefix the task outputs endpoints with /tasks
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The outputs controller exposed the task outputs directly under its root, with a
leading path variable, while the execution outputs endpoint is namespaced by
resource type. Both task outputs endpoints are now namespaced the same way:

  GET /outputs/{executionId}              -> GET /outputs/tasks/{executionId}
  GET /outputs/{executionId}/{taskRunId}  -> GET /outputs/tasks/{executionId}/{taskRunId}

Every route under the controller now has a literal second segment, so they can
no longer shadow each other and no longer depend on the route resolution
preferring a literal segment over a path variable.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(core): name the unavailable task type instead of its installed plugin on blueprints (#18204)
fix(flows): reject a file upload for an input that isn't of type FILE
historicalFixesSummary.body:
An uploaded multipart file part was bound to any input regardless of its
declared type, so e.g. an ION input silently resolved to the string
"kestra" (the start of its internal storage URI) instead of erroring like
JSON already does. Only FILE inputs now accept a file upload; every other
type is rejected with a per-input validation error.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: fix(system): make the queue INSERT query deterministic in values order
fix(system): avoid un-bounded SQL query metrics and record only above a threshold
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Add JdbcSqlSanitizer, mirroring OpenTelemetry's own db.query.text
sanitization recommendation: collapse IN/NOT IN lists to a single
element, redact quoted identifiers (aliases), and redact free-text
ORDER BY columns, so the tag's cardinality stays bounded regardless of
filter size or dashboard configuration.

Record only queries above a threshold, configured to 10ms by default.
